purpose: Postman-script byte-for-byte mimicry — test whether attachment .enc files use the same envelope shape as the working /uploadeClaims request body, and whether ZeroPadding (the asymmetric response-side decoder hypothesis) helps.
plaintext_source: PRN-1-0991013-001 (THIRTEEN) — patient identity in plaintext doesn't affect envelope-format scoring; what matters is the .enc byte shape.

files.name: CF1.pdf.enc
files.hypothesis: Canonical Postman script for binary PDFs

files.name: CF2.pdf.enc
files.hypothesis: Canonical Postman script for binary PDFs (second specimen — both PDFs same variant so any PDF success generalises)

files.name: CSF.pdf.enc
files.hypothesis: ZeroPadding asymmetric hypothesis for binary PDFs — matches PhilHealth's response-side decoder

files.name: CF4.xml.enc
files.hypothesis: Byte-identical to /uploadeClaims request envelope for XML — Postman script verbatim

files.name: eSOA.xml.enc
files.hypothesis: ZeroPadding asymmetric hypothesis for XML — matches PhilHealth's response-side decoder

decision_table.CF1.pdf.enc passes: PDFs use the canonical Postman request envelope (PKCS7). Codify.
decision_table.CSF.pdf.enc passes (and CF1/CF2 fail): PDFs use the response-side decoder (ZeroPadding). Codify.
decision_table.CF4.xml.enc passes: XMLs use the canonical /uploadeClaims request envelope. Codify.
decision_table.eSOA.xml.enc passes (and CF4 fails): XMLs use the response-side decoder (ZeroPadding). Codify.
decision_table.All five fail: Move to Round 1 — envelope shape variation (raw [IV‖ct], composite ASCII, etc.)
